A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ViLU framework and share matching original experiments. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including material moved between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original failure-detection experiments on image-label and image-caption datasets, architecture and loss ablations, transfer evaluations, and additional appendix analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains the original empirical results and adds domain-shift, five-shot adaptation, and pretraining concept-coverage experiments in Appendices C.5–C.6.

M1.justification: The core architecture and weighted-BCE objective are unchanged. New Appendix B.2 states that generalization experiments use an additional MCM-score input, but the existing transfer results remain identical. The PDFs do not establish whether this input was introduced after v1 or was previously used but undocumented; its disclosure is counted under D1.

E1.justification: Appendix C.5 adds ImageNet-V2 and ImageNet-Sketch as shifted evaluation domains for failure detection. The original 13 image-label and three image-caption datasets remain. The pooled pretraining experiment reuses 12 existing datasets rather than adding 12 new benchmarks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding original experiments, including MCM, temperature-scaled MCM, Entropy, Doctor, Rel-U, LVU, and BayesVLM where applicable. The new generalization analyses reuse MCM and LVU; LVU's five-shot condition changes its adaptation protocol rather than introducing another comparison method.

E3.justification: New protocols evaluate ImageNet-trained uncertainty models on shifted variants, both directly and after adaptation using five labeled images per class. Appendix C.6 additionally trains on pooled training sets from 12 datasets using pseudo-captions. Existing splits, metrics, caption inference batch size, and reported hyperparameter ranges are retained.

E4.justification: v4 adds focused analyses of domain-shift robustness and few-shot adaptation in Table 8, plus the effect of pretraining concept coverage in Table 9. Existing component, loss, depth, data-efficiency, batch-size, and qualitative analyses remain; the backbone study is relocated rather than newly added.

E5.justification: The revision adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures. Tables 8–9 follow the existing practice of reporting individual performance estimates.

E6.justification: All seven original numerical tables are unchanged after matching renumbered tables. New Table 8 reports, for example, ViLU ImageNet-Sketch FPR95 of 73.1 without adaptation and 54.4 with five-shot adaptation. Table 9 adds pooled-pretraining results averaging 63.1 versus 68.6 for CC12M pretraining; these are different training conditions, not revised same-setting scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, loss equations, and bilinear representation of the unnormalized MCM score are retained. Appendix B becomes B.1 with equivalent mathematics; B.2 supplies an empirical implementation explanation rather than a new derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same contributions: contextualized multimodal uncertainty representations and loss-agnostic binary failure prediction. The conclusion drops an explicit comparison with MCM and BayesVLM, but that comparative claim remains elsewhere; the central contribution and applicability claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: New discussion interprets target-domain adaptation and pretraining concept coverage as improving uncertainty generalization. Section 5.4 also strengthens its transfer statement to outperforming MCM on all 12 datasets, although unchanged Table 5 shows exceptions on CIFAR-10, Food101, DTD, and StanfordCars.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 newly discloses the explicit MCM input used for generalization, and C.5–C.6 document adaptation and pooled-data construction. An acknowledgment identifies IDRIS computing resources. Existing MLP dimensions, optimizer, learning-rate search, and batch sizes move to Appendix A.2 unchanged; repository access information is retained.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 54 works and retain the same related-work discussion and positioning against visual uncertainty predictors and probabilistic VLM approaches. Changed citation backreferences reflect relocation, not new literature.

P1.justification: v4 moves implementation details and the backbone discussion into the appendix, reorganizes appendix subsections, and rewrites several generalization explanations. Author-affiliation and acknowledgment edits are also present. The abstract and most introductory and methodological prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 adds Tables 8–9 and relocates the original backbone Table 6 as appendix Table 7. Figure 6 moves earlier, while unchanged Figures 9–10 shrink from separate pages to column-width displays on one page. The main visual design and existing graphical content are retained.

improvement.justification: The added domain-shift and adaptation tests, concept-coverage analysis, and explicit MCM-input disclosure modestly improve assessment of generalization and reproducibility. The benefit is limited: original results are unchanged, the strengthened all-12-datasets claim contradicts Table 5, and Table 9 uses target-dataset training data, so its better average does not establish improved transfer under the original training conditions.
